newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Yankee probes radioactivity report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Yankee probes radioactivity report.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Friday that its Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plant is investigating an incident of low-level radioactive contamination reported by a vendor.
Northeast shut Connecticut Yankee in July 1996 after determining the plant's containment air recirculation system was inoperable due to design definciency.
The plant's board announced in December 1996 that Connecticut Yankee would be closed permanently.
The 582-megawatt station was operated and 49-percent owned by Northeast Utilities.
Northeast said in a statement that the incident involves a return shipment of video monitoring equipment that had been used to record work evolutions in the radiological controlled area of the plant.
It said C & G Video of Oswego, N.Y., informed Connecticut Yankee on Wednesday that rental equipment returned to them from the plant had low levels of radioactive contamination.
Connecticut Yankee immediately sent representatives to C & G Video to survey the equipment.
The investigation found that some cables, a camera receiver box and other pieces of equipment had low levels of contamination, Northeast said.
Although the levels detected were "well below" regulatory requirments for reportability, Northeast said Connecticut Yankee notified the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
"The incident poses no significant health risks to personnel at C & G or to any other member of the public," Northeast said.
"I view this as a serious incident," Northeast Executive Vice President Ted Feigenbaum said.
"I have instructed that immediate steps be taken to strengthen all release controls on any material leaving the (radiological controlled area."
